name: Electrostatic Dermal Adhesion Projector
description:
The EDAP-1 projects a focused beam of ionized particles that induces a powerful electrostatic charge differential across the target's outermost dermal layer, causing them to adhere with significant force to any conductive or semi-conductive surface they contact — walls, floors, vehicle chassis, armor plating, or other people. The adhesion force scales with the surface area of contact and the conductivity of the target surface, but in typical urban environments, a fully charged target pressed against a ferroconcrete wall requires approximately 340 kilograms of force to detach. The charge dissipates naturally over four to seven minutes, or can be neutralized immediately with a grounding discharge.

The projector itself is a compact sidearm-profile weapon with a distinctive wide emitter disk at the muzzle. It fires silently, with only a faint blue corona visible at the emitter during discharge. Tessera Corponation designed it for rapid immobilization scenarios — apprehension, perimeter denial, and the specific problem of targets attempting to flee through tight urban terrain. A person adhered to a surface cannot run, and cannot easily use weapons if their hands are stuck to their sides or to each other. The weapon has a secondary 'overcharge' mode that increases the adhesion force to levels that can cause skin tearing if the target attempts to pull free, which Tessera's documentation carefully describes as 'enhanced compliance motivation.'

The street name 'Flypaper' is self-explanatory. 'The Embrace' is the term used by the GLMZ warrant enforcement community, delivered with the flat affect of people who have used it enough times that irony is no longer part of the delivery.
specifications:
effective range: 3-22m
adhesion force standard: 340 kg separation force (ferroconcrete reference surface)
adhesion force overcharge: Up to 680 kg separation force
charge duration: 4-7 minutes natural dissipation
grounding neutralization: Immediate via Tessera-compatible grounding rod
weight: 0.9 kg
power source: Integrated ionization cell, 24 standard discharges / 12 overcharge discharges
dimensions: 28cm length
tactical_use: Most effective in urban pursuit scenarios and confined-space apprehension. Operators fire on a fleeing target as they approach a wall, vehicle, or any surface, causing instant immobilization. In team operations, one operator fires while others close distance — the standard window before dissipation is more than enough for restraint application. Advanced users learn to 'layer' charges on a target who is wearing non-conductive outerwear by targeting exposed skin at the neck, hands, or face. The weapon is significantly less effective against targets with full-body non-conductive insulation, which has created a small market for anti-adhesion undersuits in communities where EDAP-1 deployment is common.
cultural_context: The EDAP-1 is one of the few exotic weapons in widespread legitimate use by licensed enforcement entities, which has given it an unusual dual reputation. For warrant officers and corporate security, it is a workday tool, worn openly and unremarkable. For the communities they operate in, it has become a symbol of a specific kind of powerlessness — the inability to run, to move, to escape — that resonates beyond its mechanical function. Anti-adhesion clothing has become a quiet form of political statement in certain districts, and the sight of someone in full insulating gear is immediately legible to anyone who knows the context. Tessera Corponation has lobbied to have anti-adhesion clothing classified as obstructing lawful enforcement.
story_hooks: A prominent activist was found adhered to the exterior wall of a building twelve stories up — the official report says they climbed there, but EDAP-1 residue says otherwise.

Tessera Corponation's grounding neutralization rods have been counterfeited in massive quantities and are flooding the black market — someone wants targets to be releasable without Tessera's knowledge or involvement.

An operator is hired to retrieve a package from a building where every surface has been pre-treated with a conductive coating, turning the entire structure into a potential adhesion trap for anyone carrying an ionized charge.

The overcharge mode on a batch of EDAP-1 units has been factory-set at maximum, and the 'compliance motivation' documentation is starting to look like a cover story for something that was always intended to injure.
